id: title:benjackwhite:restore command center task popup width

review.posthog_relevance: Desktop application command-center UI stability and usability.
review.reason: The observed change P1.F1.H1 adds a 240px minWidth style to a combobox and a corresponding test. This is a localized, bounded UI improvement. While the score is 1, the relevance is established: it prevents the dropdown from becoming too narrow, potentially improving usability for desktop users. No broader systemic changes or unverified outcomes are inferred.
review.uncertainty: The benefit is potential usability improvement rather than demonstrated; no adoption or incident avoidance is shown.

observations.limitations: This chunk is a single, cohesive change group. No unrelated PRs detected. No adoption, incident, or effort claims are supported. No tier assigned.

observations.behavior: Adds a 240px minWidth style to the combobox content and removes the inline className, while adding a test asserting that popup width is maintained.
observations.posthog_connection: Desktop app command-center: P1.F1.H1 adds a test for the TaskSelector popup width; P1.F2.H1 and P1.F2.H2 implement the minWidth style. This could help prevent the dropdown from becoming too narrow, potentially improving usability for desktop users.
